analysis:
Examined all supplied patches, BASE/HEAD source and file metadata. Release changes interact consistently: scripts/provider_release_resume/api.py:112–121 admits dev dispatches only with environment=dev, a verified commit on dev ancestry and equality to current dev head; scripts/resolve-provider-release.sh:36–42 routes these to publication, clears version overrides and forces validation_only=false. Existing production tag enforcement remains at :74–76. No demonstrated escalation into staging/prod or serving qualification (A-005, A-011, A-017, T-054); integration should verify caller ordering, signing-environment selection and resume handling for this new dispatch route.

scripts/ci-tested-tree.py:119–151 adds push reuse of tree-only records. Repository, workflow path, event, successful completion, expiration and component-superset checks remain, and errors still run tests (:156–169). For tree records, :145–146 checks only SHA syntax, not that the recording run tested the named tree. Whether artifact production provides adequate provenance requires the producing workflow and its permissions; this scope does not establish an attacker able to mint such records, so no exploit finding is asserted.

scripts/test-ci-component-paths.py patch at HEAD :327–350 and :391–436 expects opt-in PR tests, separate cluster_gpu gating, dev-push coalescing and removal of hourly coverage. Integration must inspect actual workflows/classifier and artifact publication: record flags in ci-tested-tree.py:56–57 do not encode GPU coverage, so determine whether a cluster record from a non-GPU run can suppress intended master GPU testing. Also verify required-check behavior when PR tests are skipped. These are material CI assurance questions relevant to A-017/A-018, not proven runtime regressions. Supplied changes do not directly alter encryption, cache isolation (T-041), authorization, token custody, billing or privileged helpers; missing workflow/caller evidence limits conclusions.
